matt: Quick q — procurement call ran long and I want everyone's read. We're narrowing to CostModeler vs SpendLens for next-year vendor. Main concerns: metering granularity, overage protection, renewal uplift. Any red flags?

nina: Billing note — CostModeler invoices in daily aggregated buckets which makes token-level reconciliation annoying. SpendLens gives per-request line items which maps directly to our ingestion. Also spotted a ~12% "ingress" infra fee on CostModeler we didn't expect.

alexis: Pulled a quick price snapshot for comparison:
```
CostModeler: $0.0008/token base + 12% infra fee, minimum commit $10k/mo
SpendLens: $0.00095/token, no infra fee, tiered discounts after 250M tokens
```
Link to my sheet: https://redwood-internal.sheets/example (private)

sam: Eng POV — CostModeler has a streaming-first API and a proxy-level LRU cache that reduced tail latency in our bench. SpendLens has stronger multi-region failover and slightly better SLA guarantees. Also FYI CostModeler only supports a limited set of quantized model builds which could affect eval parity.

matt: @nina @alexis can you run a 6-month forecast on our top 3 apps to show cost delta? Nina — if SpendLens reduces reconciliation effort that's a big plus for ops.

nina: Will run a usage-recon POC tomorrow. Quick Q for Alexis: does SpendLens provide programmable CSV exports or S3 hooks? We need that for GL ingestion.

alexis: Yes SpendLens has CSV export + S3 webhook. CostModeler only offers SFTP drops and a billed "reporting" addon. Vendor asked about our desired commit terms — I'm leaning to counter with a 6mo ramp + 10% renewal cap. Thoughts?

sam: From infra: hybrid makes sense — SpendLens for bulk/async workloads to simplify billing, CostModeler reserved for latency-critical endpoints. If we go hybrid, ask both for per-route pricing and a mapping table.

matt: Good tradeoffs. Action items:
- Nina: usage forecast + reconciliation-effort estimate (due EOD tomorrow)
- Alexis: draft vendor counter (10% renewal cap, S3 export + API CSV clause)
- Sam: enumerate 2-3 endpoints that truly need CostModeler low-latency path
I'll schedule a vendor follow-up for Tue 10am PT. :calendar:

procurement-bot: Reminder — vendor follow-up added to calendar (Tue 10:00 PT). Attached: vendor SLA checklist and preferred contract terms template.

nina: Ack — will have CSV export test results and a short reconability score by the call. :thumbsup:
